tools.description: What the PROVEN trader cohort is holding and trading, coin by coin. The cohort is not a guess at who is smart: it is Hyperliquid leaderboard accounts screened for provable profit (equity band, month and all-time PnL and ROI, volume-to-equity) and then verified against their own fills to trade at a cadence a person could follow. Two blocks, two different units, never added: positions_held is notional currently open, flow_traded is dollars executed inside the window (1h, 4h or 24h). Every row carries the wallet COUNT behind it and a thin flag when fewer than 3 cohort wallets are in it, because a one-wallet row is one person and not a cohort. cohort.rosterAgeHours is how old the MEMBERSHIP screen is (up to 24h), which is a separate fact from updated_at. Wallets whose live book could not be read are reported as unprofiled and are never counted as flat. Keyless. Descriptive market data only.

window.description: Which window flow_traded covers: 1h, 4h or 24h. Defaults to 24h. It does not move positions_held, which is always what the cohort holds right now, and windows_available in the reply lists what the roll-up actually published.

available.description: False when this lane could not answer: a producer is dark, the pair sits outside this plan, or the argument named something we do not carry. Absent or true means the numbers are a real reading, not a guess.

summary.description: The answer in one plain sentence, computed from the fields below. Open the reply with this, then let the numbers back it up. Null only when there was nothing to summarise.

venue.description: Which market the cohort trades on.

updated_at.description: When the roll-up was published. Separate from how old the membership screen is.

windows_available.description: The windows the roll-up actually published.

cohort.description: Who is in the cohort and how it was screened, including rosterAgeHours, the age of the membership screen.

positions_held.description: Dollars currently OPEN per coin, with the wallet count behind each row and a thin flag under 3 wallets.

flow_traded.description: Dollars EXECUTED inside the window per coin, same row shape. A different unit from positions_held and never added to it.

positions_withheld.description: How many holding rows were not returned at this access level.

flow_withheld.description: How many traded rows were not returned at this access level.

coverage.description: Which wallets could be read, and which are reported as unprofiled rather than counted as holding nothing.

note.description: One line saying what the numbers cover, or why there are none. Read it before reporting any zero as a market reading.

tools.name: market_brief
tools.title: One-call market brief
tools.description: A complete current market brief for ONE coin in a single call: price, cross-venue funding with carry, open interest, whale flow versus the coin's own baseline, recent liquidations and historical context. The plain-English name for trade_context (identical data and credit cost). Use for a general "what is happening with BTC / how is ETH positioned" question, and do not also call the separate whale, funding or liquidation tools unless the user drills into one of them. Descriptive market data only.

coin.description: Alias for pair.

pair.description: Trading pair, for example ETH/USD. A bare symbol like ETH is read as ETH/USD. Defaults to BTC/USD when omitted. On the free plans BTC answers in full and any other coin as a headline.

position_usd.description: Position size in US dollars, for example 25000. Above zero only. When given, carry_cost adds per_day_usd_at_current_rate, the dollars a day the current funding average across exchanges works out to at that size. Arithmetic on the rate as it stands now, not a projection of future rates. Omit and carry_cost still carries the percentage and APR figures.

compact.description: Return one line of plain text rather than the JSON blob, about 30 tokens instead of 800. Same facts, same windows, same dates, no structured fields to read. Defaults to false.

depth.description: Which shape came back: lite, free-pair or keyed.

stats_24h.description: The 24h statistics block. Absent on the lite shape, where locked_layers names it.

funding.description: average_rate across exchanges, how many exchanges are in it, the interval in hours, and minutes to the next funding time.

open_interest_usd.description: Open interest in dollars across the exchanges that publish it.

liquidations_recent.description: Forced closes visible right now: count, long_usd, short_usd and window_minutes. A timing series, market-wide totals run higher.

vs_own_history.description: Where funding and open interest sit against the same pair recorded days: phrase, band, day count, the date the reading is from, and how past cases resolved.

whale_flow.description: Whale direction against the same coin logged baseline: the multiple, days logged, record and N-day-high flags, and buy share now versus 7 days. Dollar sizes are added on a paid plan.

carry_cost.description: Arithmetic on the current funding average: percent per day, the same as an annual rate, which side pays, and dollars a day when position_usd was passed. Not a projection of future rates.

crowding.description: The crowding read and the overexposed side. Null without a paid plan.

price_reads.description: Plain descriptions of price against its own recent hours, computed from hourly candles: vs_recent_average (above or below its 50-hour and 200-hour average, and which way it is drifting), recent_move (how stretched the latest move is, plus the change against 7 days ago) and choppiness (calm, normal or choppy). Each block is available:true with values or available:false with a plain reason; a leg with too few recorded hours is null with a note, never a made-up neutral. Descriptive, not a trade signal.

locked_layers.description: Named rather than silently missing: which blocks this connection did not receive.

compact.description: Present and true only on a compact:true call, where the whole answer is the single line in `line`.

line.description: The composed one-line answer, returned only when compact:true was asked for. The same facts, the same windows and the same dates as the full shape.
